facts.statement: The species Argyrosaurus superbus was formally described by Richard Lydekker in 1893.
facts.quote: The type species, Argyrosaurus superbus, was formally described by Richard Lydekker in 1893.

facts.statement: The holotype of Argyrosaurus superbus is a massive left forelimb found at the Chico River in the Lago Colhué Huapi Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Argyrosaurus superbus is a huge left forelimb, MLP 77-V-29-1. found at Chico River, a Campanian/Maastrichtian horizon in the Lago Colhué Huapi Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype forelimb was originally part of a complete skeleton, but the rest of the remains were destroyed during excavation.
facts.quote: When discovered, the forelimb was apparently a part of a complete skeleton, however, during excavation the rest of the remains were completely destroyed.

facts.statement: Recent studies suggest the area where the holotype was found dates to the early late Maastrichtian rather than the early Coniacian.
facts.quote: Recent stratigraphic information from the Lago Colhue Huapi Formation has the area that the holotype was collected from being a more probable early late Maastrichtian age instead of early Coniacian.

facts.statement: The genus name means 'silver lizard' because it was discovered in Argentina, which literally translates to 'silver land'.
facts.quote: The genus name means 'silver lizard' from Greek argyros, 'silver', and sauros, 'lizard', because it was discovered in Argentina, which literally means 'silver land'.

facts.statement: Argyrosaurus was estimated to be 17 meters long and weigh up to 12 tonnes according to Paul.
facts.quote: Argyrosaurus was a medium-sized sauropod which is estimated to measure 17 m long and weighing up to 12 t according to Paul.

facts.statement: In 2012, Thomas Holtz estimated Argyrosaurus could reach 28 meters in length and weigh between 43.5 and 50.8 tonnes.
facts.quote: However, in 2012 Thomas Holtz gave a higher estimation at 28 m in length and a possible weight of 43.5-50.8 tonnes (48-56 short tons).

facts.statement: More recent estimates list Argyrosaurus at 21 meters long and 26 tonnes.
facts.quote: More recently it was listed at 21 m and 26 tonnes (28.6 short tons).

facts.statement: Argyrosaurus is distinguished by a wide ridge on the medial side of the humerus, an extremely compressed midshaft, a subtriangular distal radius, and extremely elongated metacarpals.
facts.quote: It is distinguished from other genera by the following unique features: the medial side of the humerus has a wide ridge that projects forward the midshaft of the humerus is extremely compressed the width of the distal end of the radius is only slightly greater than the midshaft width the radius is subtriangular when viewed from the distal end the metacarpals are extremely elongated

facts.statement: Argyrosaurus is classified within the family Argyrosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Argyrosauridae

facts.statement: In 2012, Argyrosaurus was placed in the family Argyrosauridae alongside the Egyptian genus Paralititan.
facts.quote: En 2012 se lo colocó en la familia Argyrosauridae junto con el género egipcio Paralititan.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Argyrosaurus may be related to Alamosaurus.
facts.quote: Aunque se sugiere que pudo estar relacionado con el alamosaurio.

facts.statement: Due to being known from few scattered bones, the morphology, size, and complete classification of Argyrosaurus are not well known.
facts.quote: Conocido por unos pocos huesos separados su morfología y tamaño no son bien conocidos, así como su completa clasificación.

facts.statement: Argyrosaurus is estimated to have reached about 21 meters in length, though some estimates suggest it could have reached 30 meters.
facts.quote: Se calcula que llegó a medir unos 21 metros de largo, aunque hay estimaciones de que llegaron hasta los 30 metros.

facts.statement: Fossils of Argyrosaurus have been found in the Bajo Barreal, Laguna Palacio, and Castillo formations in Argentina, and the Asencio Formation in Uruguay.
facts.quote: Se han encontrado pocos restos fósiles dispersos, en la Formación Bajo Barreal, la Formación Laguna Palacio y la Formación Castillo de Chubut en la Argentina y en la Formación Asencio del Uruguay.

facts.statement: Argyrosaurus was described in 1893 by English paleontologist Richard Lydekker based on a complete forelimb found by Carlos Ameghino in the Chico River of Chubut.
facts.quote: Fue descrito en 1893 por el paleontólogo inglés Richard Lydekker a partir de una extremidad anterior completa hallada por Carlos Ameghino en el río Chico de Chubut, procedente de las areniscas rojas guaraníticas de la región del lago Musters.

facts.statement: In 1978, a commission from the National University of Tucumán found new remains along the Senguerr River in Santa Cruz Province.
facts.quote: En 1978, una comisión de la Universidad Nacional de Tucumán halló nuevos restos a orillas del río Senguerr, al sur de Colonia Sarmiento, provincia de Santa Cruz.

facts.statement: A forelimb that likely belongs to this genus and a probable nest have been found in Entre Ríos Province.
facts.quote: También se ha encontrado un miembro anterior que parece pertenecer a este género y un probable nido en la provincia de Entre Ríos.

facts.statement: In 2012, Philip Mannion and Alejandro Otero argued that only the holotype remains unambiguously belong to the genus Argyrosaurus.
facts.quote: in 2012 Philip Mannion and Alejandro Otero considered the holotype remains the only material which unambiguously pertains to the genus.

facts.statement: Mannion and Otero considered the partial skeleton PLV 4628/MACN-CH 217 to be a distinct genus named Elaltitan.
facts.quote: They also considered one of the referred specimens, the partial skeleton PLV 4628/MACN-CH 217, to be its own genus which they called Elaltitan.

facts.statement: The time range for Argyrosaurus is from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Argyrosaurus was a titanosaurian sauropod that lived approximately 70 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Argentina.
rejected.quote: Argyrosaurus ( ) is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived about 70 million years ago, during the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now Argentina.

rejected.quote: The specific epithet means 'proud' in Latin.
